title: Ronald Wayne Sold 10% of Apple for $800 (10% Today: ~$500 Billion)
description:
Ronald Wayne sold his 10% of Apple for $800 in April 1976, just 12 days after he signed the partnership with Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak. As of Nov. 20, 2026, 10% of Apple's market value is about $498 billion.

Why he walked away:
- He was 41. Jobs was 21, Wozniak 25. He was the one who drew up the partnership agreement (and drew the first Apple logo and wrote the Apple I manual).
- Jobs took out a $15,000 loan to build the company's first order for a local computer store.
- In a general partnership every partner is personally liable for the debts. Wayne had a house and savings. The other two had almost nothing to lose.
- About a year later he took another $1,500 to give up any future claim. He has said he has no regrets.

The real math: Apple has issued many shares since 1976, so his original stake would have been diluted. Fortune has estimated it at anywhere from $75 billion to $400 billion depending on the assumptions.

questions.q: Why did Ronald Wayne sell his Apple shares?
questions.a: Apple was a general partnership, so each partner was personally liable for its debts, including a $15,000 loan Jobs took to fill the first order. Wayne, 41, had a house and savings at risk, so he left 12 days after signing.

questions.q: How much would Ronald Wayne's 10% of Apple be worth today?
questions.a: 10% of Apple's market value was about $498 billion at the Nov. 20, 2026 close ($4.978 trillion). Because of dilution his real stake would be smaller: Fortune has estimated $75 billion to $400 billion.
